title: Plant milk vs. cow's milk: how to compare nutrition

seo.title: Plant milk vs. cow's milk: how to compare labels
seo.meta_description: Learn how to compare plant-based milks with cow's milk for protein, calcium, vitamin D, potassium, B12, saturated fat and added sugar.
seo.search_intent: Learn how to compare plant-based beverages with dairy milk

excerpt: A plant beverage can match cow's milk for calcium through fortification while providing far less protein. Compare protein, calcium, vitamin D, potassium, B12, saturated fat and added sugar—not just calories.
content_html:
“Plant milk” covers soy, oat, almond, rice, pea, coconut and blends. The useful comparison is cow's milk versus the exact carton you buy.

Start with protein

Typical 2% dairy milk provides about 8 g protein per cup. Current unsweetened Silk soy also provides 8 g. The unsweetened almond example has 1 g and Oatly Unsweetened lists 0 g.

Calcium can match because it is added

Fortified plant beverages can equal or exceed dairy milk's calcium. Current examples list 470 mg per cup for Silk unsweet soy and almond milk and 320 mg for Oatly Unsweetened.

Check vitamin D and potassium

The FDA recommends comparing protein, calcium, vitamin D and potassium. Many products also add B12 and vitamin A.

Added sugar changes the picture

Oatly Original lists 7 g added sugar per cup while its unsweetened version lists 0 g. The word “oat” does not tell you the sugar content.

Saturated fat varies

Soy, almond and many oat drinks are low in saturated fat; coconut drinks can be much higher.

Closest replacement

Current U.S. guidance recognizes fortified soy beverage as the plant option nutritionally similar enough to dairy milk for the dairy group. For a daily replacement, look for similar protein plus meaningful calcium, vitamin D and potassium, with low added sugar.

faq.question: Which plant milk is closest in protein?
faq.answer: Fortified soy is usually closest; the Silk unsweetened example provides 8 g per cup.

faq.question: Does equal calcium mean equal nutrition?
faq.answer: No. Protein, vitamin D, potassium, B12 and other nutrients can differ.

faq.question: What should I check for a daily replacement?
faq.answer: Protein, calcium, vitamin D, potassium, B12, saturated fat and added sugar.
